clue.text: A cheat simply becomes abstruse

indicators.note: the letters of the first three words turn into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who cheats in a plain way somehow turns obscure and hard to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes' looks like a plain link verb, but it signals that A CHEAT SIMPLY is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: abstract philosophical talk about being and reality is proverbially difficult to grasp.

clue.text: Man inhales oxygen that's less dry

indicators.note: breathing in takes the gas inside the man, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Mister is the title for a man
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A man breathes in oxygen, and the air somehow becomes damper.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative synonym: something damper has more moisture and so is less dry.

clue.text: Doctor helps at mountain range

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor lends a hand at a mountain range, perhaps in a ski resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person; it is a verb signalling that HELPS AT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the great European range running through Switzerland, Austria, France and Italy.

clue.text: Friend has a supply of food that's tasty

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a table is the food provided at meals, as in 'she keeps a good table'

explanation.surface: A friend keeps a stock of delicious food.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: food that is pleasant to eat is agreeable to the palate.

clue.text: Youth leader 'appily listens a long time

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter
the dropped H in 'happily' shows a Cockney accent, which drops the H from the next word too

parts.note: hears means listens

explanation.surface: A youth leader cheerfully listens for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appily mimics the Cockney habit of dropping an initial H, so HEARS loses its H to give EARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: 'for years' means for a very long time.

clue.text: Clued up and enthusiastic about University College Hospital

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it
UCH is the abbreviation for University College Hospital, in London

explanation.surface: Someone well informed and keen on a particular London teaching hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a container signal, but 'enthusiastic about' together means INTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being well informed and up to date with what is happening.

clue.text: Messenger has porter keeping mail

indicators.note: one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale
post means mail

explanation.surface: A messenger has a hotel porter who holds onto the letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' is the drink, not a doorman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek original means 'one sent out', so an envoy or messenger of the faith.

clue.text: Expression doctor hears up front

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the following three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor listens to a patient's chest from the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is a verb signalling that HEARS UP FRONT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a particular way of putting something into words is an idiomatic expression.

clue.text: Institution has a lot that's not perfect

parts.note: a uni, a university, is an institution of learning
'a great deal' means a lot

explanation.surface: An establishment owns plenty of things that are flawed.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonym formed with a prefix: falling short of an ideal means not perfect.

clue.text: Opposed to old church in biblical town

parts.note: anti means opposed to

explanation.surface: Someone against an ancient church in a town from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the city in Acts where followers of Jesus were first called Christians.

clue.text: Ought, in more difficult circumstances, to stop here

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: harder means more difficult
should means ought

explanation.surface: A motoring rule: in tricky situations, this is the place to pull over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circumstances' completes the surface and the sense of the definition: the strip beside a motorway where a driver stops in an emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the emergency lane beside a British motorway is where a broken-down vehicle pulls in.

clue.text: Communication when school rejected sanction

indicators.note: turned back, so the school's name is read backwards

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school
to let is to allow or sanction

explanation.surface: A message sent after a school refused to approve something.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a short letter or note is a form of written communication.

clue.text: Walk in nature's strange way

indicators.note: the letters of the word before are put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Strolling in the odd manner that the natural world has.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a leisurely stroll is a kind of walk.

clue.text: Creates questionnaires

definitions.meaning: documents with blanks to be filled in

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a verb for shaping or making, and the paper documents people fill in.

clue.text: Reprobates ultimately bomb boats

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: lighters are flat-bottomed barges

explanation.surface: Villains end up bombing boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boats' are the barges called LIGHTERS, not cigarette lighters.
explanation.definitionFit: British colloquial synonym: a rotter, a contemptible person, is a bad lot or reprobate.

clue.text: Spoke to rudely about American being cut off

indicators.note: the outer piece goes round the other

parts.note: insulted means spoke to rudely

explanation.surface: Someone spoke rudely about an American who was then isolated.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being shielded or isolated from outside influences means being cut off.

clue.text: Others lie about hosts

indicators.note: here about means scattered around, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Other people tell lies about those who entertain guests.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: people who run hotels play host to their guests.

clue.text: Test authorised on reflection here in Israel

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a viva is an oral examination
let means allowed or authorised

explanation.surface: Reconsidering a sanctioned exam held somewhere in Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' looks like 'after thinking'; it turns VIVALET round.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the major coastal city in Israel, its commercial centre.

clue.text: Allow insulating material is a disappointment

parts.note: let means allow
down, soft feathers, is used to insulate duvets and jackets

explanation.surface: Permitting feather padding turns out to be disappointing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something that fails to meet hopes is an anticlimax or disappointment.

clue.text: Crew try fruit

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it
a go is a try or attempt

explanation.surface: A ship's crew tries some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a tropical stone fruit with orange flesh.

clue.text: Mike arranged siesta for artist

parts.note: Mike is the NATO alphabet word for M

indicators.note: the letters of the following word are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Mike set up an afternoon nap for a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Henri, the French painter at the heart of Fauvism.

clue.text: Operatic heroine partners French invaders

parts.note: Norma is the Druid priestess heroine of Bellini's opera
North and South are partners at bridge, N and S

explanation.surface: An opera heroine joins up with foreign raiders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partners' is the bridge pairing North and South.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the conquerors from northern France who invaded England in 1066.

clue.text: Each heavenly body belonging to an outstanding group

parts.note: all means each, as in a score of two all
a star is a heavenly body

explanation.surface: Every celestial object seems to be in a superior band.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective: made up entirely of leading performers, like a team of celebrities.

clue.text: Tree product initially stopped during check

indicators.note: one piece falls within the time of the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: to rein in is to check

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Tree sap first halted while someone held it back.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the sticky substance exuded by trees such as pines.

clue.text: Subsequently the French turned sideways

parts.note: later means subsequently

indicators.note: turned round, so the French word is read backwards

parts.note: la is the feminine form of 'the' in French

explanation.surface: Afterwards, the French turned to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lateral movement is movement to the side.

clue.text: Eastern Nevada promises to be green

parts.note: NV is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Nevada
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: Pledges made in east Nevada are bound to be environmental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' looks like environmental; it means jealous.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: 'green with envy' makes green mean jealous or covetous.

clue.text: Willing to examine a note

definitions.note: an adjective here meaning having made a will

parts.note: to test is to examine
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Ready and eager to check a musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Willing' reads as eager, but here means having made a will.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal term: a person who dies having left a valid will is described this way.

clue.text: Don appears after ironing formal wear

indicators.note: the second piece is placed following the first

parts.note: evening clothes out with an iron means ironing
to don is to put on, or dress

explanation.surface: An Oxford don turns up after the ironing, dressed up for a dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' is the verb 'put on', not a university teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: smart clothes for evening functions, such as dinner jackets and gowns, are formal wear.
